The main takeaway from our work is that
, for a large class of problems, Frank-Wolfe methods can provably converge to the global optimum with linear per-iteration computational cost.

, for a large class of problems in robust statistics and signal processing, Frank-Wolfe methods can be combined with proximal operators in a principled way to obtain scalable and provable convergent algorithms.
